book_title: Chapter 3: Basis Differentials, Well Economics & The FY2025 Cash Waterfall
question: How do EQT's firm transportation portfolio, combo-development well economics, and collar hedging program translate into sub-$1.10/Mcfe operating costs and ~$2.00/MMBtu unlevered free cash flow breakeven?

epigraph.quote: In natural gas, geology sets the ceiling on well productivity, but midstream egress and per-unit cash cost determine who survives the winter that never arrives.
epigraph.author: North American Gas Desk

web_blocks.html: Natural gas is not a global barrel like Brent crude; it is a pressurized fuel bound by pipe limits. The Appalachian Basin produces over 35 Bcf/d of U.S. supply [9, 20]. When local output tops outbound pipe capacity, local hubs like Eastern Gas South or Dominion South trade $0.50 to $1.20/MMBtu below Henry Hub [9, 20]. EQT's supply chain counters this basis penalty with three tools [1, 4]. First, it owns its gathering and compression network [1, 4]. Second, it holds firm transport deals to Gulf Coast, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic buyers [1, 4]. Third, it curtails wells when spot prices sag [1, 4].

On the drilling side, EQT runs a standardized 'combo-development' model built during Toby Rice's 2019 overhaul [16]. Rather than drilling single wells, EQT develops multi-well pads with 15,000-to-20,000-foot laterals at once [1, 3]. Crews tune frac spacing, recycle water, and use electric frac fleets [1, 3]. In Q1–Q3 2026, faster drilling cut capex ~10% below initial guidance midpoint [3, 4, 5]. Q3 2026 capex was $638 million, while full-year 2026 sales volume guidance rose to 2,375–2,450 Bcfe [3, 4, 5].

web_blocks.takeaway: EQT's total per-unit operating costs of $1.03–$1.09/Mcfe in 2026 provide a wide cash margin buffer even when Henry Hub trades near $2.50/MMBtu [3, 4, 5].

web_blocks.html: To manage cash flows across shoulder months, EQT uses rolling 12-to-18-month hedges [2]. Entering 2026, EQT held costless collars near a $3.94/MMBtu floor on ~25% of output [2]. However, the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q (as of October 20, 2026) reveals a material shift in the 2027 hedge book [5]. For Q4 2026, EQT holds 108 MMDth of collars ($3.72 put / $5.13 call) [5]. For FY2027, EQT hedged 462 MMDth (~19% of standalone volume): 228 MMDth in fixed short swaps at $3.13–$3.16/Dth (Q2–Q4) and 234 MMDth in three-way collars carrying $2.50/Dth short puts [5]. Those swaps cap summer-to-winter upside, while sold $2.50/Dth puts re-expose cash flow if Henry Hub breaks below $2.50/Dth [5]. Meanwhile, 9M 2026 basis and liquids hedges incurred $191 million in net cash settlement losses, and EQT curtailed 21 Bcfe in Q3 2026 ($2.72/Mcfe realized) [5].

web_blocks.takeaway: From $8,644.2M in FY2025 operating revenue, EQT generated $3,249.6M in operating income (37.6% operating margin), $5,126.0M in operating cash flow, and $2,802.0M in free cash flow after $2,324.0M of capital expenditures [1].

web_blocks.html: The audited FY2025 Form 10-K waterfall shows strong cash conversion [1]. Total operating revenue was $8,644.2 million [1]. That included $7,726.7 million from gas, NGL, and oil sales, plus $291.0 million in net hedge gains and midstream revenue [1]. Direct transport, processing, and production costs totaled $1,920.8 million [1]. That split into $1,532.1 million for transport and processing and $388.7 million for production expense [1]. SG&A was just $380.1 million (4.4% of revenue), while non-cash DD&A was $2,600.4 million [1]. Adding back $2,600.4 million of non-cash DD&A lifted operating cash flow to $5,126.0 million [1]. After $2,324.0 million in capex, EQT generated $2,802.0 million in organic free cash flow [1].

web_blocks.title: Unit Economics Watchpoint: Maintenance Capex vs. Decline Rates
paragraphs: Shale gas wells decline 60%–75% in year one before flattening into hyperbolic tails. Holding ~6.5 Bcfe/d on ~$2.3B annual capex relies on shallowing base declines, yet EQT also carries $13.2 billion in off-balance-sheet firm pipeline and processing demand commitments (~$1.1B/year in 2026–2027) [1, 4]. Those fixed demand charges remain payable even when EQT curtails wells, creating hidden operating-leverage friction during prolonged low-price troughs [1].

web_blocks.html: Pad-level unit economics are clear from the per-Mcfe cost bridge. In FY2025, EQT realized $3.19/Mcfe on gas, NGL, and oil sales, including cash hedges [1, 2]. Total per-unit operating costs averaged ~$1.08/Mcfe in FY2025 [1]. Those costs include gathering, transport, processing, lease operating expense (LOE), production taxes, and cash SG&A [1]. Across Q1–Q3 2026, unit costs improved to $1.03–$1.09/Mcfe [3, 4, 5]. LOE was just $0.09/Mcfe ($0.08/Mcfe in Q2 2026), and production taxes were $0.07/Mcfe [1, 4]. That left over $2.00/Mcfe of cash operating margin before maintenance capex [1, 4].

Capital intensity forms the second half of unit economics. Shale wells decline steeply in year one, so EQT must keep drilling to hold output flat at ~6.4–6.7 Bcfe/d (2,375–2,450 Bcfe/year in 2026 guidance) [4, 5]. In FY2025, capex was $2,324.0 million, or ~$0.98/Mcfe of sales volume [1, 2]. Add ~$1.08/Mcfe in cash operating costs and ~$0.18/Mcfe in net interest ($438.7 million / 2,382 Bcfe) [1]. Together with ~$0.98/Mcfe in maintenance capex, all-in sustaining cost sits near ~$2.24/Mcfe [1]. On an unlevered Henry Hub basis, that equals ~$2.00/MMBtu after NGL uplift and third-party midstream credits [1, 3].

EQT's 2027 hedge and curtailment shift alters its cash-flow profile. Rather than relying solely on wide two-way collars, EQT locked in 228 MMDth of Q2–Q4 2027 fixed swaps at $3.13–$3.16/Dth alongside 234 MMDth of three-way collars with $2.50/Dth short puts [5]. That structure reflects softer near-term strip dynamics after EIA's November 2026 STEO cut its winter 2026–2027 Henry Hub forecast 16% to $2.87/MMBtu and 2027 to $2.88/MMBtu. Curtailing 21 Bcfe in Q3 2026 (and guiding 10–20 Bcfe for Q4) still preserves Tier-1 gas in the ground, though fixed pipeline demand fees (~$1.1B/year) continue accruing during shut-ins [1, 5].

Underground storage adds another buffer against regional basis swings [1]. During mild spring and autumn months, EQT can inject excess gas into its FERC-regulated storage fields in Pennsylvania and West Virginia [1, 2]. When winter cold fronts spike Mid-Atlantic demand, EQT withdraws that gas and ships it south on MVP to capture peak pricing [3, 8, 18].

book_paragraphs: If you want to understand why so many natural gas drillers go broke even when they sit on world-class rock, you and I have to talk about pipeline physics and basis differentials. A barrel of crude oil can ride a railcar, a barge, or a truck if a pipeline fills up. Natural gas cannot. It moves only through steel pipes under pressure. When Appalachian drillers produce more than the local pipes can carry, local prices collapse relative to the national Henry Hub benchmark—sometimes by a dollar or more per MMBtu.

EQT's entire supply chain is built to defeat that geographic trap. Picture a newly completed multi-well pad in Greene County, Pennsylvania. Under Toby Rice's combo-development playbook, EQT drills multiple three-mile laterals off a single pad, using recycled water and electric frac fleets to drive down well costs [1, 16]. Once the gas hits the surface, it flows into EQT's own gathering headers, passes through centralized compression, and enters a diversified portfolio of firm transportation contracts—including the 2.0 Bcf/d Mountain Valley Pipeline—that carry molecules out of Appalachia to premium Mid-Atlantic and Gulf Coast markets [8, 18].

Look at the per-unit math from 2025 and 2026. EQT's 9M 2026 lease operating expense ticked up 11% year-over-year to $0.10 per Mcfe, and SG&A reached $0.10 per Mcfe, while production taxes held at $0.07 per Mcfe [5]. Total per-unit operating costs came in at $1.09 per Mcfe in Q1 2026, $1.03 in Q2, and $1.09 in Q3, keeping unlevered breakeven near $2.00 per MMBtu [3, 4, 5]. Still, EQT carries $1.1 billion in annual fixed pipeline demand charges and shifted 2027 hedges heavily into $3.13–$3.16 swaps and $2.50 short-put three-way collars [1, 5].

book_subsections.title: Reading the FY2025 Cash Waterfall
paragraphs: Now let us walk down the FY2025 income statement and cash flow statement line by line, because the gap between accounting profit and cash generation is the secret to EQT's deleveraging speed. In FY2025, EQT booked $8,644.2 million in total operating revenue [1]. Direct transportation, processing, and production costs consumed $1,920.8 million, and SG&A took just $380.1 million [1].

The single biggest expense on the income statement was non-cash depreciation, depletion, and amortization (DD&A) at $2,600.4 million [1]. After $493.3 million of other operating expenses, $438.7 million of net interest, $167.0 million of other income, and $651.9 million of taxes, consolidated net income was $2,326.0 million ($2,039.2 million attributable to EQT shareholders) [1].

Here is the magic for a capital allocator: because DD&A is a non-cash charge reflecting historical drilling and acquisition costs, EQT's net cash provided by operating activities surged to $5,126.0 million [1]. Subtracting $2,324.0 million in capital expenditures left $2,802.0 million in free cash flow in a single year—cash that went straight toward retiring Equitrans-era debt [1].

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: In shale gas, accounting earnings can be distorted by non-cash DD&A and mark-to-market derivative swings. The true north star is the spread between realized price and all-in cash cost, multiplied by capital efficiency.

book_subsections.title: The Pad-Level Math: Why $0.09 LOE Changes Everything
paragraphs: Let us break down the unit economics of a single thousand cubic feet equivalent (Mcfe) of gas so you can see why EQT's cost structure is so hard for rivals to match. In FY2025, EQT realized $3.19 per Mcfe across 2,382 Bcfe of sales [1, 2]. How much did it cost to lift that gas out of the ground, pay local severance taxes, move it through gathering headers, and run corporate headquarters?

Just $1.03 to $1.09 per Mcfe in 2026 [3, 4, 5]. Think about those numbers. Lease operating expense—the actual field cost of operating the wellhead, managing produced water, and maintaining surface equipment—is only $0.08 to $0.09 per Mcfe [1, 4]. Production taxes are $0.07 per Mcfe [1]. Even after paying ~$0.98 per Mcfe in annual capital expenditures to replace depleting reserves and ~$0.18 per Mcfe in net interest, EQT generates positive free cash flow at gas prices that force Haynesville and smaller Appalachian drillers to park their rigs.

And notice how management handles the inevitable shoulder-season slumps. In Q3 2026, rather than selling gas into a soft summer tape, EQT shut in 21 Bcfe of production [5]. You cannot do that with a manufacturing plant—idling a factory destroys fixed-cost absorption—and you cannot easily do it with high-water-cut oil wells without risking wellbore damage. In dry Marcellus shale, shutting a valve simply leaves the pressurized gas safely in the rock until winter prices return.

book_subsections.title: Inside the $100 Waterfall: Why Maintenance Capex & Basis Dictate Cash
paragraphs: If you only look at an E&P company's income statement, you will miss half the story—because depreciation, depletion, and amortization (DD&A) is a non-cash accounting echo of wells drilled years ago, whereas maintenance capital expenditure is the real cash check you must write every single year just to keep production flat. That is why our Chapter 3 $100 revenue-to-free-cash-flow waterfall starts at the top with audited FY2025 revenue and walks straight down to operating cash flow and capex.

Notice how lean EQT's cash operating structure remains post-Equitrans, even with 9M 2026 LOE and SG&A ticking up to $0.10 per Mcfe [5]. However, Q3 2026 filings show two frictions investors cannot ignore: basis and liquids hedges lost $191 million in cash across 9M 2026, and the 2027 hedge book pivoted to 228 MMDth of fixed swaps ($3.13–$3.16/Dth) plus three-way collars with sold $2.50/Dth puts [5]. That caps upside above $3.16 on swapped volumes while leaving downside open below $2.50/Dth—a critical nuance now that EIA's November 2026 outlook pegs 2027 Henry Hub at $2.88/MMBtu.

The second hidden lever in unit economics is basis—the price difference between Henry Hub in Louisiana and local Appalachian sales points. Historically, trapped Appalachian gas suffered $0.75 to $1.25/MMBtu basis blowouts every autumn. By owning firm transportation and Mountain Valley Pipeline capacity, EQT shrinks that basis penalty and converts geological advantage into durable free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: The Hidden Cost of Steel, Water & Compression in Appalachia
paragraphs: If you walk onto a Marcellus well pad in southwestern Pennsylvania, you immediately notice why scale is a physical moat rather than a PowerPoint buzzword. Drilling a three-mile lateral requires millions of gallons of water, thousands of tons of frac sand, high-horsepower electric or dual-fuel frac fleets, and miles of steel casing.

Smaller operators rent third-party water trucks and pay spot rates for gathering compression. EQT owns integrated water systems and the Equitrans gathering grid, spreading fixed infrastructure across massive pad volumes. That physical integration is why EQT's cash operating costs dropped to $1.03–$1.09 per Mcfe in Q1–Q3 2026—a cost floor that smaller, unintegrated peers simply cannot replicate.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: EQT's 2027 pivot toward $3.13–$3.16/Dth swaps and three-way collars with $2.50/Dth short puts—alongside $1.1B/year in fixed pipeline demand commitments—means hedging no longer provides pure uncapped upside or an absolute floor.
